header:
Date: 2027-01-11 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 49m | Location: Zoom | Record: Fireflies.ai export
Attendees: Daniel Cruz (Redwood AE), Priya Menon (Redwood SE), Omar Khalid (Redwood Solutions), Sanjay Rao (Marlin Head ML), Lena Ortiz (Marlin Eng Mgr), Marta Bell (Marlin Finance), Chris Yoon (Marlin Infra)
summary: Discovery + POC scoping focused on cost per token, batching/caching knobs, acceptable latency SLOs, and a 2-week benchmark pilot. Key constraint: finance wants a 6-month runway with conservative 95th perc latency under 300ms for chat flows; Marlin leaning toward Dedicated after pilot if unit economics meet model.
transcript:
00:00 Daniel Cruz: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're gonna spend about 45 minutes on scope. Quick intros — I'm Daniel from Redwood, AE, Priya's our SE.
00:12 Sanjay Rao: Hi, Sanjay here, Head of ML at Marlin. We're trying to scope a POC to move our product chat assistant to a hosted inference that can scale. Marta is on finance.
00:25 Marta Bell: Hi all.
00:28 Priya Menon: Great, quick agenda: confirm success criteria, look at your workload patterns, propose a benchmarking matrix (latency, cost, accuracy), and knock out next steps.
00:38 Lena Ortiz: For context, we run about 3M monthly messages today, peak 200 rps on Black Friday spikes, but normal day is closer to 20 rps. Average prompt length ~120 tokens in, 80 tokens out.
00:52 Chris Yoon: Infra note: we prefer private deployment (VPC peering) for PII redaction; SOC 2 is a requirement.
01:02 Daniel Cruz: Good. For economics, the two knobs are model choice (bigger model = higher per-token) and serving config: batching, KV cache, prefix caching. We typically model per-token cost and expected token/sec after batching.
01:18 Priya Menon: I want to flag that our Dedicated pool can be configured for steady throughput and burst; for a POC we usually spin up a small dedicated pod and run stepped load tests. That gives deterministic tail latency.
01:31 Sanjay Rao: Success for us is twofold: 1) 95th perc latency under 300ms for single-turn chat on peak-ish load (scaled test) and 2) unit cost per session <= $0.002 assuming our average session is 180 tokens. Finance will want a 6-month forecast.
01:48 Marta Bell: Yes, the runway math is critical — we need an apples-to-apples per-month spend with conservative growth.
01:55 Priya Menon: Understood. For per-token estimates we'll give best-case (with aggressive batching & prefix caching) and conservative (minimal batching); example: with model XYZ-13B quantized on our runtime you might see effective per-1k-token cost of $0.12 best-case, $0.22 conservative. These are illustrative; we'll run your exact prompts through the harness.
02:20 Lena Ortiz: Wait, can you walk through what you mean by prefix caching vs KV cache? We've heard KV cache but our infra folks mix terms.
02:30 Omar Khalid: Sure — KV cache is the key value cache for the model's past hidden states so subsequent tokens are faster; prefix caching is caching identical prompt prefixes across requests (helpful for templated prompts). In practice, prefix helps a lot for QA where the system message is static.
02:43 Chris Yoon: For us, 70% of requests reuse the same system prompt, so prefix caching could cut token cost significantly.
02:50 Daniel Cruz: Exactly. In the cost model we account for cache-hit rate. If you get 60% prefix hit and 20% KV reuse, your effective tokens billed drop meaningfully.
03:03 Sanjay Rao: How do you model batching? Our typical latency SLO for product is 150ms p50 and 400ms p95. We care about p95.
03:12 Priya Menon: We simulate different batch windows. For example, at 10 concurrent requests a 8–12ms batching window adds microseconds; at very low qps, batching hurts latency. We provide a batching policy: target latency vs cost savings curve. We'll include a chart in the model.
03:28 Marta Bell: Can you quantify how much batching reduces per-token cost for our profile? Ballpark.
03:33 Priya Menon: Ballpark: at your 20 rps steady state with 180 token sessions, intelligent batching + caching could reduce per-session token compute cost by ~30–45% versus no batching. For peak 200 rps bursts, batching yields 50% savings because of better GPU utilization.
03:52 Daniel Cruz: Important to note quantization: running a 13B in 4-bit can drop GPU cost 2–3x with modest accuracy loss. We'll include model variants in the benchmark (fp16, 8-bit, 4-bit) and measure quality delta with your eval prompts.
04:10 Lena Ortiz: We need guardrails: if quality drops more than 2% on our evals, we won't accept the quantized option.
04:16 Priya Menon: That's a good acceptance criterion; we'll add it to success metrics.
04:22 Sanjay Rao: On security, SOC 2 plus VPC peering and KMS integration are musts. Do you support customer-managed keys?
04:30 Daniel Cruz: Yes, Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM with customer-managed keys for Private deployments. For Dedicated we offer KMS integration; we can scope exact key management in the security docs. We'll send our SOC 2 and private deployment checklist after the call.
04:44 Chris Yoon: Network: during pilot we'll need an allowlist for IPs and a peering window. How disruptive is enabling peering?
04:51 Omar Khalid: Usually minimal. We provide peering docs and a short support slot to configure. We'll test connectivity before benchmark.
04:58 Sanjay Rao: For the benchmark itself, what's the recommended harness? We want a realistic distribution, not just synthetic spikes.
05:06 Priya Menon: We'll run a three-phase test: 1) steady-state baseline at your daily average scaled to tokens/sec, 2) stepped ramp to peak (20rps -> 200rps over 20m), 3) stochastic burst replay of your top-1000 session traces if you can share. Metrics: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, tail latencies, and per-1k-token cost.
05:30 Marta Bell: For finance, we'd also like projected monthly cost scenarios: conservative, expected, aggressive. Use growth rates 10% and 35% for 6 months.
05:40 Daniel Cruz: We'll produce three scenarios in the spreadsheet. We'll assume the pilot numbers and apply growth. We'll show line-item cost: model compute token cost, network egress (if any), storage for KV caches, and reserved capacity vs burst credits.
05:53 Lena Ortiz: One more: how do you handle model rollouts and canarying? We need to test A/B with our existing endpoint.
05:59 Priya Menon: Redwood supports canary rollouts and automatic fallback to a thinner model if SLOs break. For the POC we can set up a 10% routing canary from your prod traffic into the pilot environment (with sanitization). That gives real-world fidelity.
06:12 Sanjay Rao: Sounds good. Marta, anything else from finance?
06:16 Marta Bell: We'll want a clear termination cost if we scale down after pilot, and clarity on overage billing for burst. Also liability language — but legal will handle that.
06:26 Daniel Cruz: We'll include burst billing examples and a simple run-rate calculator.
06:30 Chris Yoon: Regarding observability, can you expose token-level traces and per-request cost attribution?
06:35 Omar Khalid: Yes, Redwood Console gives per-route token breakdowns, latency histograms, and traces. We'll enable a short retention for pilot logs and show you how to hook into your Splunk/DataDog.
06:47 Sanjay Rao: Let's lock timeline: We want pilot results within two weeks of kickoff. Is that realistic?
06:52 Priya Menon: Yes: Day 0-2: security & peering; Day 3-5: deploy model variants and baseline; Day 6-10: run stepped benchmarks and qualitative evals; Day 11-14: analysis + handoff. We can compress if Marlin can share traces immediately.
07:09 Daniel Cruz: So next steps recap: Sanjay to share sample prompts + traffic histogram by Fri (2027-01-14); Priya will send benchmark harness + prompts by Wed (2027-01-13); Daniel sends cost sheet and contract pilot terms by 2027-01-15; schedule a connectivity check with Chris for 2027-01-12.
07:29 Lena Ortiz: Quick question: in your per-token model, do you bill for cached tokens?
07:33 Priya Menon: We bill tokens that are executed — prefix caching prevents re-executing the model for that prefix. If a prefix hit is served from cache we only bill for the delta tokens. There are nuances for KV reuse but we'll show exact accounting in the spreadsheet.
07:50 Sanjay Rao: Any red flags?
07:52 Daniel Cruz: Only risk is if your real-world prompts deviate greatly from the samples — we'll mitigate with trace replay. Also if regulatory docs delay peering, the timeline shifts.
08:02 Marta Bell: Okay thank you. We'll review and align.
08:06 Daniel Cruz: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the deliverables.
08:09 [meeting ends]
